transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just done your post-cataract surgery follow-up check.

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

So gentle gardening is fine, but just be careful not to do anything too heavy or tiring for that first month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful. Another thing I'm wondering is when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you need a new supply, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside. That should help.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks have you had the surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. A week in, some blurriness is quite normal and should improve quickly over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision is still blurry or gets significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thanks for answering all my questions, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and well done on your recovery. Goodbye!

verdict.label: pass
